classification.difficultyReason: Calculate rectangular wall area, account for three coats, and convert the resulting coverage requirement into litres using the stated rate.

content.prompt: On a tin of paint, it states that you can cover $16\text{ m}^2$ per litre. How many litres of paint do you need to cover a rectangular wall $5.2\text{ m}$ by $2.3\text{ m}$ if you need to apply three coats? Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Wall area:
$$5.2\times2.3=11.96\text{ m}^2$$
Total area for three coats:
$$11.96\times3=35.88\text{ m}^2$$
Let $x$ be the number of litres required.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{16}{1}&=\frac{35.88}{x}\\\frac{1}{16}&=\frac{x}{35.88}\\\frac{35.88}{16}&=x\\x&=2.2425\\x&\approx2.24\end{align*}$$
Approximately $2.24\text{ L}$ of paint is required.
